summary:
Giresun province stands under the national framework of Türkiye, which Human Rights Watch describes as moving from residual prejudice toward codified hostility. A leaked omnibus draft, the 11th Judicial Package, reported on 29 October 2025, would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise LGBT conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality" with up to 3 years' imprisonment, and would criminalise same-sex ceremonies with up to 4 years. The same package would raise the eligibility age for gender-affirming healthcare from 18 to 25, impose mandatory infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, expose providers to fines and up to 7 years' imprisonment, and expose patients to up to 3 years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected to the draft.

The draft had not been enacted as of the October 2025 reporting, but its pending status does not describe the operative baseline. Türkiye has decriminalised homosexuality since the Ottoman penal code of 1858 and has permitted legal gender change and gender-reassignment surgery since 1988, so a trans visitor enters a country where transition is lawful on paper while advocacy and public expression are the targets of the current legislative push.

Entry and stay interactions carry an outing risk that follows from the absence of protective machinery. Türkiye has no comprehensive national law banning discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, does not recognise same-sex marriage, civil unions or joint adoption, and bars LGBT people from openly serving in the military. ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking placed Türkiye 47th of 49 countries.

Public visibility is the most exposed activity. Pride events have been banned in Istanbul and other cities in most years since 2015, with police deploying tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants. A visitor attending or near any Pride-related gathering in Giresun should expect the same enforcement pattern applied nationally.
tangentialFactors:
The 1858 decriminalisation of homosexuality under the Ottoman penal code indicates that the current trajectory is a political choice rather than an inherited statutory ban, which is relevant to how a visitor reads official statements in Giresun.

The 11th Judicial Package drew coordinated objection from 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association, showing that organised domestic resistance exists even where the draft's provisions are not yet in force.

ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking, which placed Türkiye 47th of 49, situates the country at the bottom of its regional comparison set and is consistent with the Pride bans recorded across multiple cities since 2015.

The Constitutional Court's overruling of the closure case against Lambda Istanbul is the one documented instance of judicial pushback against association bans, and it stands against the wider pattern of restriction.
localsOnly:
Residents of Giresun have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, and gender-reassignment surgery has been legal in Türkiye since the same year.

The pending 11th Judicial Package would raise the age threshold for gender-affirming healthcare to 25 and attach mandatory infertility and multiple-evaluation conditions, with providers facing fines and up to 7 years and patients up to 3 years — a change that falls on residents' care access rather than on visitors.

Same-sex marriage, civil unions and joint adoption are not recognised in Türkiye, and there is no comprehensive national anti-discrimination statute covering sexual orientation or gender identity, so residents have no statutory complaint route on those grounds.

LGBT people are barred from openly serving in the Turkish military, and the Constitutional Court has upheld the right of Lambda Istanbul to operate after a closure case was brought against it.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Giresun-specific finding was recorded in the source inventory for this province, so nothing in the summary is drawn from local Giresun reporting; the profile rests entirely on the national framework.

The status of the 11th Judicial Package is unresolved in the sources: it was reported as a leaked draft on 29 October 2025 and had not been passed at that point, and no later source in the inventory confirms whether it was enacted, amended or withdrawn.

Whether Giresun hosts or has banned Pride events, and whether local police in Giresun have conducted the checkpoint stops recorded in Istanbul, is not sourced and remains unverified.

The practical application of the 1988 legal gender change procedure, including documentation requirements at provincial offices in Giresun, is not covered by the inventory.
